raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`gpu_tensor_hash` computes each tile's offset as `pid * TILE` in int32. For a tensor over 8 GiB (2**31 words), the offset wraps negative and the kernel reads before the buffer: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`.

`/weights_checker` with `action=checksum` hashes every weight with this kernel, so it crashes the engine on any model with a tensor over 8 GiB per rank. We hit it on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP 8, where each rank's engram table slice is 12.3 GB.

## Modifications

- Compute the offset in int64. Tensors under 8 GiB hash to the same values as before.
- Add a test that hashes a tensor just over 8 GiB (it fails without the fix), and one that pins the hash of a small tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

The change affects hashing only, not model outputs. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (8×B300, TP 8, EP 8), the `/weights_checker` checksum failed before the fix. With the fix, it succeeds in 6.9 s and the engine stays healthy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hashing a 4 GiB tensor on a B300 takes 2.94 ms before and 2.99 ms after (about 1.7% slower). The kernel isn't on the forward path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

detail.title: [Fix] kernels: Hash tensors over 8 GiB in gpu_tensor_hash

files.patch:
@@ -56,7 +56,8 @@ def hash_tiles32_kernel_blocked(
     USE_CG: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     pid = tl.program_id(axis=0)
-    base = pid * TILE
+    # int64: pid * TILE overflows int32 past 2**31 words (8 GiB).
+    base = pid.to(tl.int64) * TILE
 
     s1 = tl.full((), seed1, tl.uint32)
     s2 = tl.full((), seed2, tl.uint32)

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.memory.gpu_tensor_hash import gpu_tensor_hash
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=20, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+
+def test_small_tensor_hash_is_unchanged():
+    tensor = torch.arange(1 << 20, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    assert gpu_tensor_hash(tensor) == 0x217789F197E070FE
+
+
+def test_tensor_over_8_gib():
+    nbytes = (8 << 30) + 4 * 8192  # one tile past 2**31 uint32 words
+    if torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0] < nbytes + (1 << 30):
+        pytest.skip("needs about 9 GiB of free GPU memory")
+    tensor = torch.zeros(nbytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    before = gpu_tensor_hash(tensor)
+    tensor[-1] = 1
+    assert gpu_tensor_hash(tensor) != before
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))
